---
title: "Hindsight"
subtitle: "Would this system have flagged real drug safety warnings before the FDA issued them?"
---

The FDA's adverse event database holds 20.7 million spontaneous reports. The
disproportionality statistics regulators screen them with are public, and so is
the list of safety warnings the FDA has actually issued.

That makes an unusual thing possible: for each real warning, recompute the
signal using **only the reports that existed before that date**, and measure how
early it would have fired. The backtest is the point. Everything before it exists
to make it trustworthy.

The misses and the false positives get published beside the hits.

## Milestones

**[M0 — Walking skeleton](reports/m0.qmd)** · One partition through every layer.
The first ranking it produced was contaminated, and measuring how badly is the
milestone's result.

M1 — the full corpus · M2 — entity resolution and deduplication · M3 — signal
detection · M4 — the backtest · M5 — dataset release. Not yet written.
